answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake behind one identity, verified through costly, rate-limited attestations from established peers. Like a juniper rooting in rocky soil, a new identity grows slowly: it earns transaction rights only as it accumulates honest history, and any fraud forfeits its stake. A flood of fakes is like a tide pushing into a narrow inlet — the bottleneck of stake and time makes mass forgery expensive, since each fake costs real funds and weeks of waiting, while one genuine agent passes cheaply.
